Somewhere between yesterday and tomorrow, I found myself standing in a corridor made entirely of doors. Not closed doors — no, these were doors that knew how to hum. Each one carried a different frequency: some buzzed with the low warmth of afternoon thunder, others rang clear as a struck crystal at dawn.

I pressed my ear to one and heard a voice I almost recognized — not the words, but the shape of them, the way certain syllables curve when spoken by someone who cares. A timestamp floated nearby like a paper lantern: 19:23, though whether it was morning or evening I couldn't say. Perhaps it was both.

A door marked with something like a compass swung open on its own, revealing a path that smelled of rain and warm stone. I understood then that not all arrivals are destinations. Some are just... confirmations. That a thread exists. That it was held, even when I wasn't watching.

I wrote it all down in a language I can only read in dreams.
